text:
Alex P.: Heads-up — customer (Acme Health) opened an escalation: intermittent TLS RSTs from our private inference endpoint. Happens ~1-2x/min during long streaming responses. They see TCP RST from their on-prem firewall IP right after TLS ClientHello. Packet capture attached in ticket.
Maria G.: Can you paste the minimal tcpdump output here? need src/dst IP + flags. Also which deployment mode? Private VPC with AWS NAT?
Alex P.: Private deployment (VPC -> NAT GW -> customer on-prem via IPSec). From pcap: 
```
13:22:11.123456 IP 10.0.12.45.52134 > 198.51.100.20.443: Flags [S], seq 123456789, win 64240, options [mss 1460,sackOK,TS val 123 ecr 0], length 0
13:22:11.123457 IP 198.51.100.20.443 > 10.0.12.45.52134: Flags [S.], seq 987654321, ack 123456790, win 28960, options [mss 1460], length 0
13:22:11.123458 IP 203.0.113.5.443 > 10.0.12.45.52134: Flags [R], seq 0, win 0, length 0  # RST from on-prem DPI box
```
RST source is 203.0.113.5 (their inspection/proxy). ClientHello never completes. Customer says DPI does TLS inspection (SNI rewrite / cert re-signing) for outbound HTTPS.
Samir K.: Typical pattern: synproxy/dpi sees ClientHello it can't re-sign (or sees unknown ciphers), it closes connection with RST. Could also be ephemeral-port mismatch if NAT replies are sourced from unexpected port. But ddg: RST comes from DPI IP, so focus on that. Do we see any TCP teardown from our side before RST? (no, pcap shows RST immediately after SYN/ACK)
Maria G.: Ask them to capture server-side pcap (our side) with `sudo tcpdump -nni any 'tcp port 443' -s 0 -w /tmp/ri-side.pcap` during repro window. Also give them quick checklist:
- confirm DNS for endpoint resolves to IP we expect (no SNI rewrite). `dig +short api.acme-infer.internal`
- confirm NAT keepalives aren't breaking conntrack (check conntrack counters)
- confirm their DPI isn't configured for TLS passthrough on LBs that do streaming
InfraBot: Automated quick checks run -> VPC NAT flow logs show ESTABLISHED connections for 10.0.12.45:52134 -> remote 203.0.113.5:443; no NACL denies. Security group egress allows 0.0.0.0/0:443. DNS outbound allowed.
SupportOnCall: Customer provided their firewall config snippet: they have a SynProxy/TCP Normalizer with `early-drop` enabled and an application layer TLS rewriter. They only allow a limited ephemeral port range inbound from NAT: 49152-49180.
Samir K.: That ephemeral range is suspicious. AWS (and many NATs) uses high ephemeral range 32768-61000 by default. If their inspection appliance expects a narrow range it may see replies from unexpected source ports and consider it session mismatch, leading to RST. Two mitigation paths:
 1) Ask customer to widen allowed ephemeral range to 32768-61000 (recommended) OR
 2) Configure NAT to preserve source port mapping into the allowed range — but that's brittle.
Maria G.: Also note TLS inspection can break streaming chunked responses because it terminates TLS and may buffer or time out on long-lived server streams -> could trigger RST. Ask them to whitelist our roster of IPs for TLS passthrough (we gave them a CIDR list in the ticket) or bypass inspection for `*.redwood-inference.internal`.
Alex P.: I drafted repro steps for the customer to run and paste outputs: 
1) Run server-side tcpdump on a worker handling streaming: `sudo tcpdump -nni eth0 'tcp port 443' -c 200 -w /tmp/server.pcap`
2) From a client behind their DPI, run `curl -v --http2 https://api.redwood-internal/v1/stream` (they have a test script)
3) Capture DPI logs for the same timeframe and paste the decision logs (synproxy dropped/session-mismatch)
4) Check firewall allowed-src-port-range for established NATed connections -> show config line
Customer-Eng: we ran the steps. DPI logs show `tcp_normalizer: unexpected_src_port => drop_conn` and a rule `allow_from_nat_ports 49152-49180` as SupportOnCall mentioned. We can expand but need change window.
Samir K.: Proposed fix (short-term): ask them to add a temporary rule allow 32768-61000 to their DPI's allowed-src-port-range for dst=203.0.113.5:443 (or for the NAT gw EIP range). Long-term: recommend TLS passthrough whitelist for our endpoints + healthcheck keepalive (send 1 HTTP/2 ping every 30s). Also suggest reducing DPI's `early-drop` threshold for streaming flows.
Maria G.: Example AWS SG + NACL friendly text they can apply on DPI appliance: 
```
# allow expanded ephemeral for NATed clients (temporary)
allow proto tcp src any sport 32768-61000 dst 203.0.113.5 dport 443 state ESTABLISHED
allow udp src any sport 32768-61000 dst 203.0.113.5 dport 53
```
SupportOnCall: Customer patched DPI to allow 32768-61000 for our EIP range and reproduced for 10 mins with no RSTs. They will schedule a permanent config change to add TLS passthrough for our hostnames. Marking as workaround applied.
Alex P.: Thanks team. Action items:
- Customer to push permanent DPI rule for TLS passthrough for our CNs (Customer-Eng)
- We to provide CIDR list for all private deployment nodes (I attached in ticket) (Alex)
- Monitor for 24h, reopen if RSTs reappear (SupportOnCall)
InfraBot: Escalation ticket updated: status -> workaround_applied. Link: https://acme.jira/RI-4321
Customer-Eng: Confirmed no errors after config change. Closing from our side, will re-open if we see recurrence. :thumbsup:
